name: Learn: RuntimeClass (sandboxing)
objective: CKS › Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities. Drill EVERY RuntimeClass corner harder than the exam: create a class and its required handler, the optional scheduling/overhead fields, select it per-pod and per-Deployment, contrast with the default runtime, layer securityContext hardening on top, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Eight strict RuntimeClass practicals: pick a sandboxed runtime per workload, layer capability-dropping + non-root for defence in depth, and fix a pod wired to a class that doesn't exist. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Create a RuntimeClass
questions.teach:
A **RuntimeClass** (`apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: RuntimeClass`) is a **cluster-scoped** object naming a container runtime the kubelet can use. Its one required field, **`handler`**, is a string the node's CRI maps to a runtime binary — e.g. gVisor's `runsc`.

**Gotcha:** `handler` is a **top-level** field, NOT under `spec` — RuntimeClass has no `spec`.
questions.prompt:
Create a cluster-scoped RuntimeClass named `gvisor` whose `handler` is `runsc`.

Target: `kubectl get runtimeclass gvisor` exists and its `.handler` is exactly `runsc`.
questions.hint: `apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1`, `kind: RuntimeClass`, `metadata.name: gvisor`, and a top-level `handler: runsc` (NOT under spec). `kubectl apply -f -`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: gvisor
handler: runsc
YAML

questions.title: A RuntimeClass with scheduling + overhead
questions.teach:
A RuntimeClass can carry optional fields the scheduler honours: **`scheduling.nodeSelector`** steers its pods onto nodes that actually have the runtime, and **`overhead.podFixed`** reserves resources the sandbox itself consumes. Both sit alongside the top-level `handler`.

**Gotcha:** `scheduling` and `overhead` are **top-level** on the RuntimeClass (siblings of `handler`), not inside a pod spec.
questions.prompt:
Create a RuntimeClass named `kata` with:
- `handler` = `kata`
- `scheduling.nodeSelector` = `{ runtime: kata }`
- `overhead.podFixed` = `{ memory: 64Mi, cpu: 50m }`

Target: `kata` has handler `kata`, that nodeSelector, and that podFixed overhead.
questions.hint: All three are top-level fields on the RuntimeClass object: `handler:`, `scheduling: { nodeSelector: {...} }`, `overhead: { podFixed: {...} }`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: kata
handler: kata
scheduling:
  nodeSelector:
    runtime: kata
overhead:
  podFixed:
    memory: 64Mi
    cpu: 50m
YAML

verification.description: RuntimeClass 'kata': handler kata + scheduling.nodeSelector runtime=kata + overhead.podFixed mem 64Mi/cpu 50m

questions.title: Run a pod on a RuntimeClass
questions.teach:
A pod opts into a RuntimeClass via **`spec.runtimeClassName: <name>`** — a pod-level field. `kubectl run` has no flag for it, so inject it with `--overrides='{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}'`, or just write the YAML.

**Gotcha:** since `runsc` isn't installed here the pod won't actually run on gVisor — we grade only that `.spec.runtimeClassName` is set, not the phase.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `runtimeclass-learn`, create pod `sandboxed` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) requesting the `gvisor` RuntimeClass via `spec.runtimeClassName`.

Target: pod `sandboxed` has `.spec.runtimeClassName` = `gvisor`.
questions.hint: `kubectl run sandboxed -n runtimeclass-learn --image=busybox:1.36 --overrides='{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}' --command -- sleep 3600`, or apply YAML with `spec.runtimeClassName: gvisor`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: sandboxed, namespace: runtimeclass-learn }
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

questions.title: Contrast with a default-runtime pod
questions.teach:
RuntimeClass is per-workload: sandbox the sensitive pods, leave the rest on the node's default runtime (usually `runc`), which shares the host kernel directly. A pod with **no `runtimeClassName`** uses that default.

**Gotcha:** `-o jsonpath='{.spec.runtimeClassName}'` returns an **empty string** for a default-runtime pod — that emptiness is the correct "normal" state, not a mistake.
questions.prompt:
In `runtimeclass-learn`, create pod `normal` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) with **no** `runtimeClassName`.

Target: `normal` exists with an empty `.spec.runtimeClassName`, while `sandboxed`'s is still `gvisor` — the two differ.
questions.hint: `kubectl run normal -n runtimeclass-learn --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600` — no overrides. Leaving runtimeClassName unset selects the default runtime.

verification.description: 'normal' has empty runtimeClassName while 'sandboxed' has gvisor (they differ)

questions.title: Harden the sandboxed pod (defence in depth)
questions.teach:
A sandbox is one layer — stack **securityContext** hardening for defence in depth: **drop ALL capabilities** (container `securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`) and **run non-root** (`runAsNonRoot: true` + `runAsUser: 1000`), while keeping `spec.runtimeClassName: gvisor`.

**Gotcha:** `capabilities` is **container-level** — putting it in the pod `securityContext` is a silent no-op.
questions.prompt:
Replace pod `sandboxed` in `runtimeclass-learn` so it still requests `runtimeClassName: gvisor` AND its container drops **ALL** capabilities and runs non-root (`runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 1000`). Keep image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`.

Target: `sandboxed` has runtimeClassName `gvisor`, `runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 1000`, and its container's `capabilities.drop` contains `ALL`.
questions.hint: Delete and re-apply YAML with `spec.runtimeClassName: gvisor`, pod `securityContext: { runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 1000 }`, and the container's `securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`. busybox sleep runs fine as uid 1000.
questions.solution:
kubectl delete pod sandboxed -n runtimeclass-learn --ignore-not-found
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: sandboxed, namespace: runtimeclass-learn }
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
YAML

verification.description: 'sandboxed' keeps gvisor AND runs non-root (uid 1000) AND drops ALL caps

questions.title: Select a RuntimeClass from a Deployment
questions.teach:
For controllers, `runtimeClassName` lives in the **pod template** — `spec.template.spec.runtimeClassName` — so every replica gets the sandbox. It is NOT a field on the Deployment's own `spec`.

**Gotcha:** setting it at `deployment.spec.runtimeClassName` (outside the template) is rejected/ignored — it must be inside `template.spec`.
questions.prompt:
In `runtimeclass-learn`, create a Deployment `sandboxed-web` with 2 replicas, container `c` running `nginx:1.25`, whose pod template requests `runtimeClassName: gvisor`.

Target: Deployment `sandboxed-web` has 2 replicas and `.spec.template.spec.runtimeClassName` = `gvisor`.
questions.hint: Put `runtimeClassName: gvisor` under `spec.template.spec` (sibling of `containers`), not on the Deployment spec. Set `spec.replicas: 2`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: sandboxed-web, namespace: runtimeclass-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: sandboxed-web } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: sandboxed-web } }
    spec:
      runtimeClassName: gvisor
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: nginx:1.25
YAML

questions.title: List and confirm both classes coexist
questions.teach:
A cluster can expose **several** RuntimeClasses so workloads pick the isolation they need; `kubectl get runtimeclass` lists them all. The class **name** (what pods reference) and the **`handler`** (what the CRI maps to a binary) are separate fields.

**Gotcha:** deleting a RuntimeClass does NOT touch pods already referencing it — they keep their `runtimeClassName` string, which simply won't resolve on the next schedule.
questions.prompt:
Confirm the cluster exposes BOTH classes you built: `gvisor` (handler `runsc`) and `kata` (handler `kata`), coexisting.

Target: `kubectl get runtimeclass` lists both `gvisor` and `kata` with their correct handlers (`runsc` and `kata`).
questions.hint: This passes once steps 1 and 2 are done. Verify with `kubectl get runtimeclass` and `kubectl get runtimeclass gvisor kata -o jsonpath='{.items[*].handler}'`.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod wired to a RuntimeClass that doesn't exist
questions.teach:
A pod naming a `runtimeClassName` the cluster doesn't have is rejected with **RuntimeClass … not found** and never schedules. `kubectl describe pod

` shows the bad name. Fix it to an existing class. **Gotcha:** `runtimeClassName` is **immutable** on an existing pod — you must delete and recreate the pod with the correct class name; editing it in place is rejected.
questions.prompt:
Pod `brokenrc` in `runtimeclass-learn` won't schedule — its `runtimeClassName` names a class that doesn't exist. Diagnose the fault and fix it so the pod references a VALID existing RuntimeClass (`gvisor`). Keep image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`.

Target: pod `brokenrc` exists with `.spec.runtimeClassName` = `gvisor` (a class that actually exists). (As in step 3, the runsc handler is absent so the pod stays Pending — we grade the corrected spec, not the phase.)
questions.hint: `kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn describe pod brokenrc` → runtimeClassName is a typo (`gvisro`). runtimeClassName is immutable, so `kubectl delete pod brokenrc` and recreate it with `runtimeClassName: gvisor`.
questions.solution:
# describe shows runtimeClassName 'gvisro' (typo) — the class doesn't exist.
kubectl -n runtimeclass-learn delete pod brokenrc --ignore-not-found
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: brokenrc, namespace: runtimeclass-learn }
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

verification.description: 'brokenrc' is Running with a valid runtimeClassName gvisor (typo fixed)
